idiom_name: mutex-protected partial-result table + condition variable collector
implementation_notes: C has no futures or channels in the standard library, so the classic stateful filter is written directly: a mutex-protected table of partial results keyed by correlation id, an expected-count field, and a pthread_cond_t that the merging thread waits on until the completeness condition (count reached or deadline passed) holds; the merge then runs in that thread and the aggregate is handed to the output queue before the entry is freed. POSIX pthread_mutex_lock/pthread_cond_wait/pthread_cond_timedwait provide the synchronization, and the same lock must cover both the table update and the completeness check so a partial cannot arrive between them. The classic structure stays the right shape whenever sub-messages arrive from independent threads or processes and completion is decided by arrival count rather than by a single join point.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_wait must be called with the mutex held and re-checked in a while loop (spurious wakeups); a single if lets the collector merge an incomplete aggregate.
Each correlation entry must be freed exactly once on both the completion and the timeout path, or the table leaks one entry per lost partial.
A single global mutex serializes every aggregate: partition the table by correlation-id hash and use pthread_cond_timedwait per partition once fan-in grows.
